question: Which of the following Articles deals with the Right against Exploitation? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Articles 31–32
Articles 25–28
Articles 29–30
Articles 23–24
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Articles 23–24

Explanation:
The Right against Exploitation in the Indian Constitution is enshrined in Articles 23 and 24. Article 23 prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and beggary, while Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 in factories, mines, or hazardous industries. These fundamental rights protect citizens from all forms of exploitation, ensuring social justice and human dignity. They are part of Part III of the Constitution. The other options: Articles 31–32 (Right to Property and Constitutional Remedies), Articles 25–28 (Right to Freedom of Religion), and Articles 29–30 (Cultural and Educational Rights of Minorities) are incorrect. Thus, Articles 23–24 are the correct answer.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Articles dealing with Right against Exploitation → 23 and 24
☛ Article 23 prohibits → human trafficking and forced labor
☛ Age limit for child labor prohibition under Article 24 → below 14 years
☛ Hazardous industries mentioned in Article 24 → factories, mines, etc.
☛ Part of the Constitution where these rights are found → Part III (Fundamental Rights)
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा अनुच्छेद शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार से संबंधित है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)

अनुच्छेद 25-28
अनुच्छेद 29-30
अनुच्छेद 23-24
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 23-24

Explanation:
शोषण के विरुद्ध अधिकार भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 23 और 24 में वर्णित है। अनुच्छेद 23 मानव के दुर्व्यापार और बालश्रम पर रोक लगाता है। अनुच्छेद 24 14 वर्ष से कम उम्र के बच्चों को खतरनाक उद्योगों में काम करने से प्रतिबंधित करता है। यह मौलिक अधिकार नागरिकों को मानव तस्करी, बंधुआ मजदूरी और बाल श्रम जैसे शोषण से बचाता है। संविधान के भाग 3 में शामिल ये अनुच्छेद मानवीय गरिमा और समानता सुनिश्चित करते हैं। अन्य विकल्प: अनुच्छेद 31-32 (संपत्ति और संवैधानिक उपचार), अनुच्छेद 25-28 (धर्म की स्वतंत्रता), अनुच्छेद 29-30 (अल्पसंख्यकों के अधिकार) से संबंधित हैं। इसलिए, सही उत्तर अनुच्छेद 23-24 है।

question: Which of the following statements is correct about Article 323B of the Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: It permits tribunals for matters like taxation, land reforms, and labour disputes.
It allows the creation of tribunals only for the armed forces.
It restricts tribunals to environmental cases only.
It empowers states to establish tribunals for local governance.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It permits tribunals for matters like taxation, land reforms, and labour disputes.

Explanation:
Article 323B empowers state legislatures to establish tribunals for specific subjects such as taxation, land reforms, labour disputes, public services, customs, excise, sales tax, rent control, and banking. This article differs from Article 323A, which deals with administrative tribunals at the federal level. Under Article 323B, both the central and state governments can create tribunals, but it is not restricted to armed forces or environmental cases only. It does not authorize states to set up tribunals for local governance; instead, it covers a wide range of specified matters. Therefore, the correct option is the one that includes taxation, land reforms, and labour disputes, as these are explicitly mentioned under Article 323B.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was Article 323B added? → By the 42nd Amendment in 1976
☛ What tribunals can be created under Article 323B? → Tax, land reforms, labour, public services, etc.
☛ Who has the ordinance power under Article 323B? → State Legislature
☛ Difference between Article 323A and 323B? → 323A only administrative tribunals; 323B for many subjects
☛ Who oversees tribunals under Article 323B? → High Courts and Supreme Court
question_hi: संविधान के अनुच्छेद 323B के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: यह कराधान, भूमि सुधार और श्रम विवाद जैसे मामलों के लिए न्यायाधिकरणों की अनुमति देता है।
यह केवल सशस्त्र बलों के लिए न्यायाधिकरणों के निर्माण की अनुमति देता है।
यह न्यायाधिकरणों को केवल पर्यावरणीय मामलों तक सीमित करता है।
यह राज्यों को स्थानीय शासन के लिए न्यायाधिकरण स्थापित करने का अधिकार देता है।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है यह कराधान, भूमि सुधार और श्रम विवाद जैसे मामलों के लिए न्यायाधिकरणों की अनुमति देता है।

Explanation:
अनुच्छेद 323B राज्य विधानमंडलों को कराधान, भूमि सुधार, श्रम विवाद, सार्वजनिक सेवाएं, सीमा शुल्क, उत्पाद शुल्क, बिक्री कर, किराया नियंत्रण, और बैंकिंग जैसे विषयों के लिए न्यायाधिकरण स्थापित करने का अधिकार देता है। यह अनुच्छेद 323A से भिन्न है, जो संघीय स्तर पर प्रशासनिक न्यायाधिकरणों से संबंधित है। अनुच्छेद 323B के तहत, केंद्र और राज्य दोनों न्यायाधिकरण बना सकते हैं, लेकिन यह केवल सशस्त्र बलों या पर्यावरण तक सीमित नहीं है। यह स्थानीय शासन के लिए न्यायाधिकरण स्थापित करने का अधिकार नहीं देता, बल्कि विशिष्ट विषयों के लिए देता है। इस प्रकार, सही विकल्प वह है जो कराधान, भूमि सुधार और श्रम विवाद जैसे मामलों को शामिल करता है।

question: Which of the following subjects falls under the Concurrent List? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Banking
Criminal law
Defence
Police
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Criminal law

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List. The Concurrent List includes subjects on which both the central and state governments can legislate. Criminal law (which includes the Indian Penal Code, Criminal Procedure Code, etc.) falls under the Concurrent List. Banking and Defence are in the Union List, while Police is a State List subject. Other subjects in the Concurrent List include education, forests, labour welfare, marriage and divorce, etc. In case of a conflict between central and state laws on a concurrent subject, the central law prevails as per Article 254 of the Constitution.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ How many subjects are in the Concurrent List? → 47 (originally 52, later reduced)
☛ Which subject related to education is in the Concurrent List? → Education (added in 2005)
☛ Which subject comes under the Union List? → Banking, Defence, Foreign Affairs, Atomic Energy, etc.
☛ Which subject comes under the State List? → Police, Agriculture, Local Government, Public Health, etc.
☛ If there is a conflict between central and state law on a Concurrent subject, which law prevails? → Central law (as per Article 254 of the Constitution)
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विषय समवर्ती सूची के अंतर्गत आता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: बैंकिंग
आपराधिक कानून
रक्षा
पुलिस
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है आपराधिक कानून

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की सातवीं अनुसूची में तीन सूचियाँ हैं - संघ सूची, राज्य सूची और समवर्ती सूची। समवर्ती सूची में वे विषय शामिल हैं जिन पर केंद्र और राज्य दोनों सरकारें कानून बना सकती हैं। आपराधिक कानून (जिसमें भारतीय दंड संहिता, आपराधिक प्रक्रिया संहिता आदि शामिल हैं) समवर्ती सूची के अंतर्गत आता है। बैंकिंग और रक्षा संघ सूची में हैं, जबकि पुलिस राज्य सूची का विषय है। समवर्ती सूची में शिक्षा, वन, श्रम कल्याण, विवाह और तलाक, आदि भी शामिल हैं। यदि केंद्रीय और राज्य कानूनों में विरोध होता है, तो केंद्रीय कानून प्रभावी होता है।

question: Which of the following is a classification of economic activities undertaken by the Central Statistical Organisation (CSO) in India?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Classification Code of India-2000
National Industrial Classification-1998
Industrial Classification Structure-2005
National Code for Agriculture and Industrial Classification-2009
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is National Industrial Classification-1998

Explanation:
The Central Statistical Organisation (CSO) in India issues the National Industrial Classification (NIC) for classifying economic activities. The first version of NIC was introduced in 1970, and its fourth revision was released in 1998. This classification is based on the International Standard Industrial Classification (ISIC). NIC-1998 divides economic activities into 17 sections, 88 two-digit groups, and 417 three-digit classes. It is used for compiling national income, industrial production, and employment statistics. Other options like Classification Code of India-2000, Industrial Classification Structure-2005, and National Code for Agriculture and Industrial Classification-2009 are not used by CSO.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Year of first NIC version → 1970
☛ International classification on which NIC-1998 is based → ISIC
☛ Number of sections in NIC-1998 → 17
☛ Year of latest NIC revision → 2008

question: Which schedule of the Citizenship Act, 1955, contains the qualifications for naturalisation? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Third Schedule
First Schedule
Second Schedule
Tenth Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Third Schedule

Explanation:
The Third Schedule of the Citizenship Act, 1955 contains the qualifications for naturalisation. Naturalisation is a process by which a foreign citizen can acquire Indian citizenship. The applicant must have resided in India for at least 12 years, including the last 12 months immediately preceding the application. Additionally, the applicant must not be in the service of any foreign government, must be of good character, and must take an oath to uphold the Constitution of India. The Third Schedule details all these conditions for naturalisation.

question: According to the principle of collective responsibility in India’s parliamentary system, a successful no-confidence motion against a single Union Minister requires which action? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Lok Sabha is immediately dissolved.
The entire Council of Ministers must resign.
Only the targeted minister must resign.
The President dismisses only the targeted minister.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The entire Council of Ministers must resign.

Explanation:
In India's parliamentary system, the principle of collective responsibility is enshrined in Article 75(3). It means the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. If a no-confidence motion passes against a single minister, it is considered a vote of no-confidence against the entire government. This is because ministers make decisions collectively and are accountable for each other's actions. Consequently, a successful no-confidence motion against one minister requires the resignation of the entire Council of Ministers. This system ensures executive accountability and maintains government stability. Dissolving the Lok Sabha or dismissing only the targeted minister contradicts this principle.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

question: If an RTI applicant is aggrieved by the Public Information Officer’s decision (or lack of response), within how many days must the first appeal be filed under Section 19 of the RTI Act? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: 15 days
90 days
30 days
60 days
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 30 days

Explanation:
Under Section 19(1) of the RTI Act, 2005, if an applicant is aggrieved by the decision (or lack of response) of the Public Information Officer (PIO), they can file a first appeal. This appeal must be filed within 30 days from the date on which the decision is received or should have been received by the applicant. If the appellant provides a satisfactory reason for the delay, the appellate authority may admit the appeal even after 30 days, but the total period cannot exceed 45 days. The first appeal is made to an appellate authority, who is a senior officer to the PIO. The appeal can be filed in physical or electronic form. This provision ensures that applicants have a timely remedy against unsatisfactory responses from PIOs.

☛ Can first appeal be filed after 30 days? → Yes, with valid reason up to 45 days
☛ Before whom is the first appeal filed? → Appellate authority (senior officer to PIO)
☛ What is the time limit for second appeal under RTI Act? → 90 days from the decision of first appeal

question: Select the correct statement regarding the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India. (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 3)

solution:

Explanation:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India is a statutory body established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act passed by Parliament. It is not a constitutional body. The NHRC investigates human rights violations and suggests measures to the government for their prevention.

question: Which of the following options correctly lists the composition of the State Executive in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (01/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Governor, Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
President, Governor and Chief Minister
Governor, Deputy Minister and State Council of Advisors
Governor, Chief Minister and State Legislative Assembly members
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor, Chief Minister and Council of Ministers

Explanation:
The State Executive in India, as per Articles 153 to 167 of the Constitution, consists of the Governor (constitutional head), Chief Minister (real executive head), and Council of Ministers. The Governor is appointed by the President of India, while the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor after proving majority in the Legislative Assembly. The Council of Ministers, headed by the Chief Minister, aids and advises the Governor and is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly. The President is part of the Union Executive, not the State Executive. The Deputy Minister and State Council of Advisors are not constitutional components of the State Executive. Members of the Legislative Assembly belong to the Legislature, not the Executive.

question: Which authority can dissolve the Council of Ministers at the state level? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Prime Minister
President
High Court
Governor
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Governor

Explanation:
Under Article 164 of the Indian Constitution, the Governor is the authority who can dissolve the Council of Ministers at the state level. The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and the Council of Ministers aids and advises the Governor in the exercise of his functions. The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor and the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Governor. If the Council loses majority or if the Governor believes it is not functioning according to the Constitution, he can dissolve it. This power is exercised by the Governor without the advice of the Prime Minister or the President, but it is usually invoked only in a constitutional crisis. Hence, the Governor holds the power to dissolve the state Council of Ministers.

question: Which of the following Articles deals with the rights of citizenship at the commencement of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 7
Article 10
Article 11
Article 5
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 5

Explanation:
Article 5 of the Indian Constitution defines the rights of citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution (January 26, 1950). It states that every person who has his domicile in India and who was born in India, or either of whose parents was born in India, or who has been ordinarily resident in India for not less than five years immediately before such commencement, is a citizen of India. Article 6 covers citizenship of migrants from Pakistan, Article 7 deals with citizenship of migrants to Pakistan, Article 8 covers persons of Indian origin residing outside India, Article 9 provides that a person who voluntarily acquires citizenship of a foreign state shall cease to be a citizen, Article 10 ensures continuity of citizenship rights, and Article 11 empowers Parliament to make laws regarding citizenship.

question: Which of the following Ministries is responsible for granting Indian citizenship by naturalisation? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Ministry of Law and Justice
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
Ministry of External Affairs
Ministry of Home Affairs
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ministry of Home Affairs

Explanation:
According to the Citizenship Act, 1955, the authority to grant Indian citizenship by naturalisation lies with the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). This ministry handles all matters related to citizenship including registration, naturalisation, and issuance of citizenship certificates. Although the Ministry of External Affairs deals with Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) and Non-Resident Indians (NRI) matters, the power of naturalisation rests solely with the Ministry of Home Affairs. Additionally, the Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019 was also implemented under MHA. Hence, the responsibility of granting Indian citizenship by naturalisation falls under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

question: Which of the following is NOT a role of the President of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Passing bills into laws

Conducting elections
solution:

Explanation:
The roles of the President of India include passing bills into laws, appointing the Prime Minister, and summoning and dissolving Parliament. However, conducting elections is not a role of the President; it is the responsibility of the Election Commission of India. The President is the head of state and performs certain executive, legislative, and judicial functions under the Constitution. The Election Commission ensures free and fair elections independently.

1919

question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: It deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha.
It defines the distribution of powers between the Union and States.
It contains provisions regarding Official Languages.
It provides for disqualification of members on grounds of defection.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It provides for disqualification of members on grounds of defection.

Explanation:
The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution is also known as the Anti-Defection Law. It was added in 1985 by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment. Its purpose is to prevent Members of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies from switching political parties, thereby ensuring government stability. The schedule provides for the disqualification of a member if they voluntarily leave their party or vote against party instructions. However, there are exceptions such as party mergers or decisions by the Speaker/Chairperson. The final authority to decide on disqualification lies with the Speaker or Chairperson, and their decision can be challenged in court through judicial review.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान की दसवीं अनुसूची के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान की दसवीं अनुसूची को दलबदल विरोधी कानून के नाम से भी जाना जाता है। इसे 1985 में 52वें संविधान संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। इसका उद्देश्य सांसदों और विधायकों को राजनीतिक दल बदलने से रोकना है ताकि सरकारों की स्थिरता बनी रहे। यह अनुसूची किसी सदस्य को स्वेच्छा से पार्टी छोड़ने या पार्टी के निर्देशों के विरुद्ध मतदान करने पर अयोग्य ठहराने का प्रावधान करती है। हालांकि, पार्टी विलय या स्पीकर/सभापति द्वारा निर्णय के कुछ अपवाद हैं। अध्यक्ष या सभापति को अयोग्यता पर अंतिम निर्णय लेने का अधिकार है, और इस निर्णय को न्यायिक समीक्षा में चुनौती दी जा सकती है।

question: Who among the following is the appointing authority of District Judges in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following best reflects Judicial Activism? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Declaring elections null and void
Passive interpretation of laws
Voluntary interference by the judiciary in public interest
Only enforcing existing laws strictly
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Voluntary interference by the judiciary in public interest

Explanation:
Judicial activism refers to the proactive role of the judiciary in safeguarding public interest, often going beyond its traditional limits. Unlike judicial review, which examines the constitutionality of laws, judicial activism involves courts taking suo motu cognizance of issues to ensure social justice, fundamental rights, and good governance. Key examples include the Supreme Court's intervention in pollution control, checking executive inaction, and monitoring anti-corruption investigations. Options 1, 2, and 4 reflect judicial restraint, where the judiciary remains passive or strictly adheres to existing laws. Therefore, the best reflection of judicial activism is voluntary interference by the judiciary in public interest, as it captures the essence of a proactive and socially conscious judiciary.

भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 243Q नगरपालिकाओं के गठन से संबंधित है। यह संविधान के भाग IXA में आता है, जिसे 1992 के 74वें संविधान संशोधन द्वारा जोड़ा गया था। इस अनुच्छेद के अनुसार, प्रत्येक राज्य में तीन प्रकार की नगरपालिकाओं का गठन किया जाता है: नगर निगम (बड़े शहरों के लिए), नगर पालिका परिषद (छोटे शहरों के लिए) और नगर पंचायत (ग्रामीण-शहरी संक्रमण क्षेत्रों के लिए)। नगरपालिकाओं का गठन राज्य सरकार द्वारा अधिसूचना द्वारा किया जाता है। इसके अलावा, अनुच्छेद 243W नगरपालिकाओं की शक्तियों और कार्यों से संबंधित है, अनुच्छेद 243Z वित्त आयोग से और अनुच्छेद 243P परिभाषाओं से।

question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: First Amendment Act, 1951
Seventeenth Amendment Act, 1964
Twenty-ninth Amendment Act, 1972
Fourth Amendment Act, 1955
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is First Amendment Act, 1951

Explanation:
The Ninth Schedule to the Indian Constitution was added by the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951. This schedule was created to protect land reform and certain other laws from judicial review. Under Article 31B, laws placed in the Ninth Schedule cannot be challenged in court even if they violate fundamental rights. This amendment also added Article 31A, which provides protection to land reform laws. However, in the landmark case of Kesavananda Bharati (1973), the Supreme Court established that laws in the Ninth Schedule can still be subject to judicial review if they violate the basic structure of the Constitution. Later, in the I.R. Coelho case (2007), the court clarified that any law added to the Ninth Schedule after 1973 must not violate fundamental rights.

☛ What is the purpose of the Ninth Schedule? → Protect land reform laws from judicial review
☛ Article 31B relates to? → Validity of laws in the Ninth Schedule

☛ When was the First Amendment enacted? → 1951

question: To be eligible for membership of a State Legislature, a candidate must meet which of the following qualifications as laid down in the Representation of the People Act, 1951? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)

solution:

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to make laws relating to the acquisition and termination of the Indian Citizenship? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 12
Article 10
Article 7
Article 11
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 11

Explanation:
Article 11 of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to make laws regarding the acquisition and termination of citizenship. Part II of the Constitution (Articles 5 to 11) deals with citizenship. Articles 5 to 10 determine citizenship at the time of commencement of the Constitution, while Article 11 gives Parliament the power to regulate citizenship by law. Under this power, Parliament enacted the Citizenship Act, 1955, which lays down rules for acquisition (by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, incorporation of territory) and termination (renunciation, termination, deprivation) of citizenship. Article 12 defines the State, and Article 10 relates to the continuance of citizenship under a foreign citizenship ordinance. Hence, the correct answer is Article 11.

question_hi: भारतीय संविधान का निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा अनुच्छेद संसद को भारतीय नागरिकता के अधिग्रहण और समाप्ति से संबंधित कानून बनाने का अधिकार देता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)

अनुच्छेद 7

Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 11

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 11 संसद को नागरिकता के अधिग्रहण और समाप्ति से संबंधित कानून बनाने का अधिकार देता है। संविधान के भाग II में अनुच्छेद 5 से 11 तक नागरिकता के प्रावधान हैं। अनुच्छेद 5 से 10 संविधान लागू होने के समय नागरिकता का निर्धारण करते हैं, जबकि अनुच्छेद 11 संसद को भविष्य में नागरिकता कानून बनाने का अधिकार प्रदान करता है। इसी अधिकार के तहत संसद ने 1955 में नागरिकता अधिनियम पारित किया, जिसमें नागरिकता प्राप्त करने (जन्म, वंश, पंजीकरण, देशीयकरण, क्षेत्र समावेशन) और समाप्ति (त्याग, परित्याग, वंचना) के नियम हैं। अनुच्छेद 12 राज्य की परिभाषा देता है, अनुच्छेद 10 विदेशी नागरिकता अध्यादेश से संबंधित है। इस प्रकार सही उत्तर अनुच्छेद 11 है।
